title: The darkness is not dark (Psalm 139:11–12)
hook: the night shines as the day to you

segments.voice: Yesterday, comforted to comfort: the God of all comfort, and the river that keeps moving. Your line was pass the comfort on. Who did you pass it to? Day one thousand four hundred eighteen.

The power goes out. The fridge stops humming, the screens die, and the room you know by heart becomes a room you don't. You stretch out a hand for the wall. A chair leg finds your shin. Voices drop a little in the dark. There's an old song that goes right into that moment, and further, into the other kinds of dark: the sleepless hours before dawn, the year nobody could see the way through. It's a psalm whose heading names David, and in the middle of it the singer says something strange about the dark. Today: the darkness is not dark.

Psalm 139 starts with being known: "O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me." Then it turns into a kind of hide and seek, and the singer tries every hiding place there is. "If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there." Up, down. Then the wings of the morning, and the uttermost parts of the sea. Even there. And then the last hiding place, the dark. In the King James words: "If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee." Readers hear the singer two ways here. Some hear someone trying to hide, hoping the dark will cover them. Others hear someone afraid the dark will swallow them whole. Either way, the answer is the same. Notice where the light comes from. No dawn arrives in the psalm, no lamp is lit. The night is light about the singer because the night isn't dark to God. God sees in it as in the day. And a few lines later the psalm goes to one more dark place, the womb, where, it says, I was made in secret. The singer's life began in the dark, and God was there too. So for those who pray this psalm, the dark isn't empty. It may still be dark. But it isn't empty.

Here's the practice: sit in a dark room calmly. If you can, dim the lights or turn them off. If you can't, just close your eyes. Settle, and breathe. Let the dark be what it is. Notice the sounds that get louder, the edges that disappear. If something in your life feels dark right now, let it come in too, without trying to fix it. If you pray, you can say the psalm's line slowly: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee. If you don't, simply rest in the dark and notice how this small piece of it feels. The bell holds the time.
The darkness is not dark. Psalm 139's claim that there is no hiding place from God, not even the night, because the night shineth as the day.

howItsDone: Christians pray Psalm 139 in personal prayer and in worship, and in churches that pray night prayer, evening psalms and prayers ask for God's presence through the dark hours.

original.note: Hebrew: darkness, the word in Psalm 139:11–12.

trapdoor: what you thought: God will take the dark away.
what it means: the dark isn't dark to God, so there is no place, not even the night, where God isn't.
what a scholar hears: the dark is the last hiding place the singer tries, after heaven, hell and the sea, and the answer is that darkness and light are both alike to God.

notes: Hebrew חֹשֶׁךְ (darkness), and the trapdoor's claim that 139:12 reads literally 'darkness does not darken' (lo yachshikh), both need a Keeper check.
'Made in secret' paraphrases 139:15 ('when I was made in secret'); the link of the womb to the dark is drawn from 139:13–15 and is the writer's framing.
Two readings of 139:11 (hiding vs being swallowed) are attributed to 'readers'; Keeper to confirm.
The heading 'A Psalm of David' is given as 'a psalm whose heading names David', without claiming authorship.
howItsDone mentions night prayer (e.g. Compline) generally; confirm.

Editor pass: match pair corrected to KJV 139:10 'even there shall thy hand lead me'; cut the Hebrew wordplay claim and Genesis 1:2 note; hook's hospital image replaced to avoid repeating nearby hooks.

Audit (2026-10-02): removed the claim that the psalm "doesn't say" the lights come back on and the matching myth; 139:11b ("even the night shall be light about me") does speak of light, so the teach now says the light comes from the night not being dark to God. Myth item replaced. Earlier notes about a lo yachshikh trapdoor claim are stale (that claim was cut). Psalm 139:12 was also cited on day 1411; angle here is different.
